title: Stonebridge POC — Infosec field notebook
body:
Purpose and audience:
Quick internal field notebook capturing the Stonebridge POC security workshop, questionnaire responses we hand-assembled, and the evidence mapping for the initial audit ask. Audience: solutions eng, secops, customer security reviewers, and the audit intake team.

Executive summary (short):
- Stonebridge (fintech) is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for transaction-enrichment models. They ran a 2-week POC. Primary asks: data isolation, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs for key lifecycle events, and proof of tenant separation.
- This notebook records workshop minutes (08/21–08/29), our answers to their security questionnaire, and a prioritized list of evidence artifacts we can deliver quickly vs. items requiring engineering work.

Scope we discussed:
- Inbound data: JSON payloads with PII tokens (no raw PAN).
- Model outputs: non-sensitive except enrichment labels; need retention controls and purge policy.
- Deployment target: Redwood Dedicated in customer VPC (shared tenancy but dedicated cluster).
- Controls of interest: KMS integration, RBAC, audit logging, network zoning, change management.

Attendees (workshop calls):
- Stonebridge: Kate Hollis (CISO), Omar Riaz (Platform), Sanjay Mehta (AppSec)
- Redwood: Ava Martinez (SE, owner), Liam O'Connor (infosec eng), Priya Singh (solutions), Marcus Liu (runtime eng)
- Ad hoc: Jonah Park (customer success)

Key Q&A highlights (raw notes):
1) KMS/HSM support
- Q: Can customer bring their own KMS/HSM to Dedicated?
- A (Liam): Yes — Dedicated supports external KMS via KMIP for on-prem HSMs and cloud-KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for envelope encryption. Need to confirm support for customer-managed key rotation hooks (open item).
- Evidence requested: key rotation log snippet, KMS config sample, KMIP connection test results.

2) Audit logging and retention
- Q: Where are audit logs stored and who can access them?
- A (Priya): Control plane logs sent to customer-managed SIEM or Cloud Logging; control plane access role required. App/runtime logs can be configured to stream to S3 or GCS in customer account for Dedicated. Retention policy configurable per customer (default 30d).
- Evidence requested: sample log record (anonymized), IAM role policy snippet, architecture diagram.

3) Tenant isolation and network controls
- Q: How do you enforce network isolation between tenants on Dedicated?
- A (Marcus): Pod-level namespace isolation, per-customer VPC peering, and iptables/NSG rules. For strict workloads we recommend VPC-only Dedicated nodes.
- Evidence requested: network diagram, segmentation test (tcpdump snippet), sample NACL rules.

4) Data-at-rest and in-transit
- Q: TLS, minimum cipher suite, storage encryption?
- A: TLS 1.2+ enforced; storage encrypted using customer or provider-managed keys; database volumes encrypted at rest.
- Evidence requested: TLS config excerpt from runtime, cert rotation process doc.

5) Change management and incident response
- Q: How are runtime patches and emergency fixes handled?
- A: Standard change window + emergency P0 process documented; SRE runbooks referenced.
- Evidence requested: change window calendar screenshot, incident postmortem template example.

Evidence inventory (current state, quick wins vs. blockers):
- Quick deliverables (can produce in ~2 business days):
  - anonymized audit log sample (control-plane-auth-success-20250828.log) — AVAILABLE (sanitized snippet ready)
  - architecture diagram (dedicated-vpc-segmentation-v1.png) — AVAILABLE
  - IAM role policy snippet for log ingestion (iam/log-ingest-policy.txt) — AVAILABLE
  - TLS cipher suite statement (tls-min-cipher.txt) — AVAILABLE

- Medium effort (1–2 sprints):
  - KMS rotation proof (rotation-events-202407.log) — PENDING (requires hook logs from KMIP adapter)
  - Automated network segmentation test run (seg-test-run-202508) — PENDING (SRE test harness update)

- Blockers (engineering/infra required):
  - HSM-backed key import verification report (requires customer test HSM) — BLOCKED
  - Encrypted KV audit for model cache (kv-cache-audit) — BLOCKED (adds tracing in runtime)

Workshop minutes (condensed chronologically):
- 08/21 kickoff: aligned on scope and evidence ask (KMS, logs, tenant isolation). Stonebridge provided SOW and a 45-question security questionnaire.
- 08/22 deep-dive: runtime networking presentation (Marcus) + preliminary architecture sketch. Action: send diagram and sample iptables rules (Ava).
- 08/25 hands-on lab: walked through Dedicated provisioning in test VPC; noted missing KMIP credentials for HSM test (customer action).
- 08/28 review: delivered anonymized log sample and IAM snippet. Agreed to prioritize KMS rotation evidence next.

Mapping of questionnaire items to artifacts (short crosswalk):
- Q15 (Key lifecycle) -> artifact: iam/log-ingest-policy.txt; pending: rotation-events-202407.log
- Q22 (Network segmentation) -> artifact: dedicated-vpc-segmentation-v1.png; pending: seg-test-run-202508
- Q31 (Audit trail access) -> artifact: control-plane-audit-sample-20250828.log
- Q37 (Patch process) -> artifact: change-window-calendar.png; linked_artifacts: JIRA-OPS-310

Open actions (owner + next step):
- Ava: Draft KMIP test plan and circulate to Stonebridge (due 2025-09-05) — ticket JIRA-SEC-9899
- Liam: Pull rotation events log sample from KMIP adapter and redact PII (due 2025-09-10)
- Marcus: Run network segmentation test in staging and attach pcap (due 2025-09-12)
- Priya: Prepare customer-facing Evidence Bundle (zip) and checklist; coordinate delivery (due 2025-09-07)

Risks and notes flagged during workshop:
- Risk: Customer requires HSM attestation (FIPS-140-2 cert) before pilot — may push timeline if third-party hardware validation needed.
- Note: Stonebridge will likely request SOC2-type evidence; we should not claim SOC2 compliance on behalf of Dedicated nodes until legal confirms.

Temporary mitigations suggested to Stonebridge (for pilot):
- Use application-level tokenization to limit PII exposure in payloads while we complete HSM work.
- Shorten log retention on the control plane to 7 days for pilot dataset and provide immediate export to customer-owned bucket for auditing.

Customer follow-ups (customer asks that need clarification):
- Confirm whether rotation webhook can be sent to their on-prem webhook (they prefer push vs. poll).
- Clarify retention SLA for runtime trace logs (they asked for 180 days during pilot).

Delivery checklist (what we'll hand over in Evidence Bundle v1):
- anonymized control-plane audit sample (control-plane-audit-sample-20250828.log)
- dedicated VPC segmentation diagram (dedicated-vpc-segmentation-v1.png)
- IAM policy snippet for log ingestion (iam/log-ingest-policy.txt)
- TLS cipher statement (tls-min-cipher.txt)
- Workshop minutes (this doc exported PDF)

Recommended next steps (owner):
1) Produce rotation-events sample or document timeline for when this will be available (Liam).
2) Run and capture network segmentation test (Marcus).
3) Prepare a one-page customer summary that explains temporary mitigations and expected ETA for hardening items (Priya).
4) Legal to review any language about third-party attestations before we label artifacts as ‘certified’ (Jonah to coordinate).

Appendix — quick references and links used in calls:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/STONEBRIDGE-POC
- Slack thread: #stonebridge-poc (see pinned messages for key artifacts)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/457 (adds KV audit tracing prototype)

Notes to self:
- When assembling Evidence Bundle, prefer timestamped filenames and a manifest file. Keep sensitive fields redacted and include a redaction log.
- If customer requests HSM attestation, route to partnerships for vendor contacts (we've used Thales and Utimaco previously).

End of notebook.

(If this doc looks okay, I'll convert to a customer-facing Evidence Bundle checklist and start the artifact assembly. — Ava)
